title: Commentaries of Proclus on the Timaeus, Vol. 2
author: Proclus (Taylor trans)
description: Commentaries of Proclus on the Timaeus of Plato, Volume 2, translated by Thomas Taylor (London, 1820), completing his English version of Proclus's monumental commentary. This volume continues the exposition of Timaeus's cosmology: the creation of the World Soul and its harmonic composition from the mixture of Same, Other and Being, the circles of the Same and Other and the planetary motions, time as the moving image of eternity, the creation of the stars and the celestial gods, the speech of the Demiurge to the young gods, and the formation of human souls and their vehicles. Proclus interweaves mathematics, harmonics, astronomy and theology, with appeal to Orphic, Chaldean and Pythagorean authorities. With Volume 1, it is a key source for late Neoplatonic cosmology and for the esoteric reading of the Timaeus that shaped Renaissance and modern thought.
